# Hash-pinned install set for the root Dockerfile's runtime dependency layer.
#
# Direct requirements: the whole of requirements.txt -- flask>=3.1.3,<4
# duckdb>=1.5.5 truststore>=0.10.4 certifi>=2024.2.2 pytest>=9.1.1
# pytest-playwright>=0.9.0 requests>=2.34.2
#
# `RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt` is what this file
# replaces. `docker build -t clawmetry .` is a documented way to run this
# project (README, CLAUDE.md "Deploy"), and that layer resolved seven ranges
# live at build time -- `flask>=3.1.3,<4` and `certifi>=2024.2.2` among them,
# floors that span years of releases. Two identical `docker build` invocations
# a week apart could bake different bytes into the image an org then runs.
#
# This is the same argument the FROM line already makes for the base image
# (pinned by digest, see its comment) and that docker-otel.txt makes for the
# layer directly above this one. This was the larger of the two unpinned
# resolves in the file: 27 packages against docker-otel.txt's 2.
#
# Deliberately a SEPARATE file rather than hashes added to requirements.txt.
# That file is the manifest a pip user installs from and setup.py derives
# from; adding --hash lines to it would force every `pip install -r
# requirements.txt` on any interpreter to match hashes resolved for the
# image's 3.14, which is a different closure. Same names, different
# resolution, so separate files -- and `tests/test_docker_runtime_pin.py`
# is what keeps the two from drifting apart.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash -- so the image gets the exact
# artifacts this file names, or the build fails. Every transitive dependency
# is present because --require-hashes demands the whole closure; that is why a
# 7-name manifest expands to the 27 below.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (wheels for each platform, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that
# matches any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the builder
# resolving to the same wheel this file was generated against -- an arm64
# laptop and an amd64 runner both build from this file.
#
# On the interpreter: the base image is python:3.14-slim, so this closure was
# resolved for CPython 3.14 on Linux. `truststore` is present because its
# `python_version >= "3.10"` marker applies there; a set regenerated for an
# older interpreter would legitimately differ, which is the reason this file
# is scoped to the image rather than shared with a CI job's set.
#
# NOTE on what is still unpinned in this file's Dockerfile: the `pip install
# -e .` layer further down installs the package itself, and with it the
# setup.py dependencies requirements.txt does not carry (waitress,
# cryptography, websocket-client, cffi). Those still resolve live. Pinning
# them means pinning setup.py's own closure, which is a different set with a
# different reason to change, so it is left for its own change rather than
# folded in here.
#
# Regenerating, on Linux to match the image:
#   pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --report r.json \
#     --python-version 3.14 --only-binary=:all: --target /tmp/t \
#     -r requirements.txt
# then, for each resolved name==version, take every sha256 under `urls` in
# https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json.
#
# Updating: the `/.github/requirements` pip entry in .github/dependabot.yml
# advances this file and rewrites the --hash lines along with the version, so
# a bump arrives already verifiable. Without that entry the pin would simply
# freeze the image at today's CVEs, which is the other end of the same
# problem the unpinned ranges were at.
